Refine only Chrysothemis's head and face so she reads as Electra's adult sister with her own individual face. Subject: Chrysothemis, a clearly adult Greek woman about thirty in Sophocles's palace account, speaking her own answer to Electra. Her distinctive soft square olive face has thoughtful brown eyes, gently arched brows and a short straight nose. Dark chestnut hair is drawn into a low braided knot. She wears a full-length cream linen gown, a muted plum-grey wool wrap with a simple woven edge, a narrow cloth belt and practical leather sandals. One hand holds the wrap near her waist; the other opens in a measured low speaking gesture toward image-left. Her expression is careful, composed and quietly firm. Her mature adult features and individual face read clearly.
